title.en: Manco Capac, a Stone and a Half Tall: The Idol Found in 1559
title.zh: 半身高的石像:1559年尋獲的曼科遺石

region.en: Ynti-cancha and Bimbilla, near Cuzco (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫斯科因蒂-坎恰與賓比利亞村(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham 1907

source.work: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 14, trans. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1907

summary.en: Feeling the approach of death, and fearing that his son might not retain the sovereignty because of the tyranny he had established, Manco Ccapac ordered the ten lineages that had come with him from Tampu-tocco to form a garrison to watch over his son and descendants, and to elect the successor nominated by the father. He left the bird indi in its cage, the tupac-yauri or sceptre, the napa and the suntur-paucar to his son Sinchi Rocca. Thus died Manco Ccapac, at the age of 144 years according to his lineage's accounts. They say that he was a man of good stature, thin, rustic, cruel though frank, and that in dying he was converted into a stone of a height of a vara and a half. The stone was preserved with much veneration in the Ynti-cancha until the year 1559, when the licentiate Polo Ondegardo being Corregidor of Cuzco found it and took it away from where it was adored and venerated by all the Incas, in the village of Bimbilla near Cuzco. From his time began the idols huauquis - an idol or demon chosen by each Inca for his companion and oracle which gave him answers; that of Manco Ccapac was the bird indi. He instituted the first ayllu, called Chima Panaca Ayllu; the members of this ayllu always adored the statue of Manco Ccapac. They carried it in their wars, thinking that it secured the victories they won; they also took it to Huanacauri for the huarachicos; Huayna Ccapac took it with him to Quito and Cayambis, and afterwards it was brought back to Cuzco with the dead body of that Inca.
summary.zh: 曼科·卡帕克自知死期將至,又恐因自己所行暴政,兒孫難以保住江山,便命自坦波-托科同來的十個世系結成衛隊,永遠護衛其子子孫孫,並在父王指定的繼承人死後負責推舉。他把籠中的「因蒂」鳥、圖帕克-亞烏里權杖、納帕聖羊與孫圖爾-保卡爾,一併傳給兒子辛奇·羅卡。曼科·卡帕克遂卒——按其世系所記,享年144歲。相傳他身量頎長,清瘦粗獷,兇殘而直率;死時化為一根半「瓦拉」高的石頭。此石供奉於因蒂-坎恰,備受印加王族崇敬;至1559年,庫斯科行政長官波羅·翁德加爾多在庫斯科附近的賓比利亞村將它尋出移走。自曼科之世起,歷代印加王各有「瓜烏基」神偶——選定的伴身偶像與神諭,能作答問;曼科的瓜烏基便是那隻「因蒂」鳥。他又立第一個阿伊柳,稱「奇馬·帕納卡」;此世系成員只拜曼科一人的石像。戰時他們抬著石像出征,相信它保佑勝利;行瓦拉奇庫禮時抬往瓦納考里;瓦伊納·卡帕克出征基多與卡揚比也帶著它,後來又隨王的遺體一同運回庫斯科。

sensitivity.note: The petrified founder as ancestral oracle; Polo's 1559 discovery is the archival moment when the mummy cult met the colonial state.

passages.text: They say that he was a man of good stature, thin, rustic, cruel though frank, and that in dying he was converted into a stone of a height of a vara and a half. The stone was preserved with much veneration in the Ynti-cancha until the year 1559 when, the licentiate Polo Ondegardo being Corregidor of Cuzco, found it and took it away from where it was adored and venerated by all the Incas, in the village of Bimbilla near Cuzco.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 14 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

passages.text: From this Manco Ccapac were originated the ten ayllus mentioned above. From his time began the idols huauquis, which was an idol or demon chosen by each Inca for his companion and oracle which gave him answers. That of Manco Ccapac was the bird indi already mentioned. The members of this ayllu always adored the statue of Manco Ccapac, and not those of the other Incas. They carried it in their wars, thinking that it secured the victories they won. They also took it to Huanacauri, when they celebrated the huarachicos of the Incas. Huayna Ccapac took it with him to Quito and Cayambis, and afterwards it was brought back to Cuzco with the dead body of that Inca.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 14 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: Sir Clements Markham, History of the Incas (Hakluyt Society, 1907)

title.en: Do Not Be Sorrowful: The Sun Appears to the Childless Inca
title.zh: 勿憂傷:太陽顯現於無嗣的老王

region.en: Ynti-cancha, House of the Sun, Cuzco (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫斯科太陽之屋因蒂-坎恰(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham 1907

source.work: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 16, trans. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1907

summary.en: One day Lloqui Yupanqui being very sad and afflicted, the Sun appeared to him in the form of a person and consoled him by saying: 'Do not be sorrowful, Lloqui Yupanqui, for from you shall descend great Lords'; also that he might hold it for certain that he would have male issue. For Lloqui Yupanqui was then very old, and neither had a son nor expected to have one. This having been made known, and what the Sun had announced to Lloqui Yupanqui having been published to the people, his relations determined to seek a wife for him. His brother Manco Sapaca, understanding the fraternal disposition, sought for a woman who was suitable for it. He found her in a town called Oma, two leagues from Cuzco, asked for her from her guardians, and, with their consent, brought her to Cuzco. She was then married to Lloqui Yupanqui. Her name was Mama Cava, and by her the Inca had a son named Mayta Ccapac.
summary.zh: 一日,利亞基·尤潘琪愁苦不已。太陽竟以人形顯現,安慰他道:「勿憂傷,利亞基·尤潘琪!你將有偉大的子孫。你必得男子之嗣,此為定數。」其時利亞基·尤潘琪已屆高齡,本以為無子可望。太陽之言傳布民間之後,親族們便決意為他尋一位妻子。其兄曼科·薩帕卡體察兄弟之意,在庫斯科兩萊格外一個名為奧馬的小鎮尋得合適女子,向其監護人求親,得其同意,攜歸庫斯科,嫁與利亞基·尤潘琪。她名喚瑪瑪·卡瓦;印加王由此得子,名「馬雅塔·卡帕克」。

sensitivity.note: Solar annunciation to a dynasty in crisis; the Sun as personal speaker within the royal cult.

For Lloqui Yupanqui was then very old, and neither had a son nor expected to have one.

title.en: Born with Teeth After Three Months: Mayta Capac the Child-Hercules
title.zh: 三月而生、出生有齒:大力士馬雅塔·卡帕克

region.zh: 庫斯科谷地(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham 1907

source.work: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 17, trans. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1907

summary.en: Mayta Ccapac, the fourth Inca, is to those Indians what Hercules is to us, as regards his birth and acts, for they relate strange things of him. His father, when he was begotten, was so old and weak that every one believed he was useless, so that they thought the conception was a miracle. His mother bore him three months after conception, and he was born strong and with teeth; he grew at such a rate that in one year he had as much strength and was as big as a boy of eight years or more. At two years he fought with very big boys, knocked them about and hurt them seriously. The natives hold this to be so true that they would kill anyone who asserted the contrary. When he was of very tender years he was playing with boys of the Alcabisas and Culunchimas: he hurt many of them and killed some; one day, drinking or taking water from a fountain, he broke the leg of the son of a Sinchi of the Alcabisas. The Alcabisas, unable to endure longer the naughtiness of Mayta Ccapac, determined to regain their liberty and to venture their lives for it: they selected ten resolute Indians to go to the House of the Sun and enter it with the intention of killing Lloqui Yupanqui and his son. Mayta Ccapac was in the courtyard playing at ball; when he saw enemies entering with arms he threw one of the balls and killed one, did the same to another, and attacked the rest, so that they all fled wounded. The inhabitants of the valley united to make war on the Incas; there was a battle and the Alcabisas and Calunchimas were finally defeated. Again they challenged Mayta Ccapac: as they advanced such a hail storm fell over the Alcabisas that they were defeated a third time and entirely broken up; Mayta Ccapac imprisoned their Sinchi for the remainder of his life.
summary.zh: 第四位印加王馬雅塔·卡帕克,就其出生與行事而言,於印第安人猶如赫拉克勒斯之於我們——關於他的奇事甚多。相傳他父親年邁力衰,眾人皆以為已無生育之能,故此番受孕堪稱神蹟;其二,其母受孕三月便誕下他,他出生便強健有齒;其三,他生長神速,一歲之時,體格氣力已如八歲以上的孩童;兩歲便與大孩子角力,把他們摔打致傷。土人對此深信不疑,誰敢否認便要殺誰。他幼時與阿爾卡比薩、庫倫奇馬的男孩玩耍,傷人無數,甚至殺了幾個;一日從泉邊取水,竟折斷了阿爾卡比薩辛奇之子的腿。阿爾卡比薩人不堪其擾,決意以死爭回自由:選出十名悍勇之士,持械闖入太陽之屋,欲殺利亞基·尤潘琪父子。馬雅塔·卡帕克正在院中玩球;見敵持械入內,擲球殺一人,又殺一人,再驅其餘——來犯者帶傷而逃。谷中居民聯合討伐印加人,大戰一場,阿爾卡比薩與庫倫奇馬終被擊潰。他們再挑戰端:進軍之際,天降冰雹,專擊阿爾卡比薩軍,致其第三次慘敗潰散;馬雅塔·卡帕克將其辛奇終身監禁。

sensitivity.note: The three-month gestation hero-birth; Sarmiento explicitly compares him to Hercules.

passages.text: Mayta Ccapac, the fourth Inca, son of Lloqui Yupanqui and his wife Mama Cava, is to those Indians what Hercules is to us, as regards his birth and acts, for they relate strange things of him. At the very first the Indians of his lineage, and all the others in general, say that his father, when he was begotten, was so old and weak that every one believed he was useless, so that they thought the conception was a miracle. The second wonder was that his mother bore him three months after conception, and that he was born strong and with teeth. All affirm this, and that he grew at such a rate that in one year he had as much strength and was as big as a boy of eight years or more. At two years he fought with very big boys, knocked them about and hurt them seriously... they hold this to be so true that they would kill anyone who asserted the contrary.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 17 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

passages.text: They say of this Mayta that when he was of very tender years, he was playing with some boys of the Alcabisas and Culunchimas, natives of Cuzco, when he hurt many of them and killed some. And one day, drinking or taking water from a fountain, he broke the leg of the son of a Sinchi of the Alcabisas, and hunted the rest until they shut themselves up in their houses.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 17 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

passages.text: The Alcabisas, unable to endure longer the naughtiness of Mayta Ccapac, determined to regain their liberty and to venture their lives for it. So they selected ten resolute Indians to go to the House of the Sun where Lloqui Yupanqui and his son Mayta Ccapac lived, and enter it with the intention of killing them. At the time Mayta Ccapac was in the court yard of the house, playing at ball with some other boys. When he saw enemies entering the house with arms, he threw one of the balls he was playing with, and killed one. He did the same to another, and, attacking the rest, they all fled... There was a battle between the two armies and although it was doubtful for some time, the Alcabisas and Calunchimas were finally defeated by the troops of Mayta Ccapac. Again they challenged Mayta Ccapac to battle, which he accepted. As they advanced they say that such a hail storm fell over the Alcabisas that they were defeated a third time, and entirely broken up. Mayta Ccapac imprisoned their Sinchi for the remainder of his life.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 17 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: Sir Clements Markham, History of the Incas (Hakluyt Society, 1907)

title.en: He Dared to Open the Hamper: The Oracle of the Bird Indi
title.zh: 敢啟箱籠者:因蒂神鳥的神諭

region.zh: 庫斯科因蒂-坎恰(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham 1907

source.work: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 17, trans. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1907

summary.en: They relate of Mayta Ccapac that he dared to open the hamper containing the bird indi. This bird, brought by Manco Ccapac from Tampu-tocco, had been inherited by his successors, the predecessors of Mayta Ccapac, who had always kept it shut up in a hamper or box of straw, such was the fear they had of it. But Mayta Ccapac was bolder than any of them. Desirous of seeing what his predecessors had guarded so carefully, he opened the hamper, saw the bird indi and had some conversation with it. They say that it gave him oracles, and that after the interview with the bird he was wiser, and knew better what he should do, and what would happen.
summary.zh: 相傳馬雅塔·卡帕克竟敢打開藏「因蒂」鳥的箱籠。此鳥乃曼科·卡帕克自坦波-托科攜來,歷代先王奉為傳家之寶;歷代諸王懼之甚深,始終將它鎖在草編箱籠之內。唯有馬雅塔·卡帕克膽氣過人:他急欲一睹先王守護如此之秘,遂啟箱籠,得見因蒂鳥,並與之交談。相傳神鳥向他降下神諭;自那番晤談之後,他變得更為明智,深知當行之事、將來之事。

sensitivity.note: The oracular bird as royal familiar; the taboo-breaking opening of the dynastic relic.

title.en: Inca Rocca Divides the Waters: The Birth of the Hanan-cuzcos
title.zh: 印加·羅卡分水:哈南庫斯科世系之立

region.en: Cuzco, upper and lower waters (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 庫斯科上水與下水(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Inca tradition as given to Sarmiento de Gamboa, 1572; trans. Markham 1907

source.work: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa, History of the Incas, ch. 19, trans. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1907

summary.en: When Ccapac Yupanqui died, Inca Rocca, his son by his wife Ccuri-hilpay, succeeded. This Inca Rocca showed force and valour at the beginning of his Incaship, for he conquered the territories of Muyna and Pinahua with great violence and cruelty, rather more than four leagues to the south-south-east of Cuzco. He killed their Sinchis Muyna Pancu and Huaman-tupac, though some say that Huaman-tupac fled and was never more seen. He did this by the help of Apu Mayta his nephew. He also conquered Caytomarca. He discovered the waters of Hurin-chacan and those of Hanan-chacan - the upper and lower waters of Cuzco - and led them in conduits, so that to this day they irrigate fields. While his ancestors had always lived in the lower part of Cuzco, and were therefore called Hurin-cuzcos, he ordered that those who sprang from him should form another party, and be called Hanan-cuzcos, the Cuzcos of the upper part. So from this Inca began the party of upper or Hanan-cuzcos, for he and his successors left their residence at the House of the Sun and established themselves in the upper part of the town, building palaces. Each Inca had a special palace in which he lived, the son not wishing to reside in the palace where his father had lived; it was left with servants, relations, ayllus or heirs that they might maintain it, and keep the edifices in repair.
summary.zh: 卡帕克·尤潘琪駕崩,其子印加·羅卡繼位。羅卡初登大位便顯示武力:以暴烈手段征服庫斯科東南偏南四萊格外的穆伊納與皮納瓦之地,誅其辛奇穆伊納·潘庫與瓜曼-圖帕克(一說瓜曼-圖帕克出逃,自此無蹤),其侄阿普·馬雅塔效力其間。他還征服了卡伊托馬爾卡。他又勘明庫斯科的「下水」與「上水」(烏林-查坎與哈南-查坎),鑿渠引水灌溉——至今其子孫猶受其利。其先祖世居庫斯科下城,故稱「烏林庫斯科」;他則下令:出自自己的子孫另立一支,稱「哈南庫斯科」——上庫斯科。自此,印加王族遷出太陽之屋,在城之上部營建宮室而居。每位印加王皆有專屬宮殿,子不居父宮;父王駕崩,宮殿原樣留存,由僕從、親族與阿伊柳子孫奉養修葺。

sensitivity.note: The Hanan/Hurin institutional split located in this reign; Sarmiento's version against those who date it to Pachacuti.

passages.text: This Inca Rocca showed force and valour at the beginning of his Incaship, for he conquered the territories of Muyna and Pinahua with great violence and cruelty. They are rather more than four leagues to the south-south-east of Cuzco. He killed their Sinchis Muyna Pancu, and Huaman-tupac, though some say that Huaman-tupac fled and was never more seen. He did this by the help of Apu Mayta his nephew... He also conquered Caytomarca. He discovered the waters of Hurin-chacan and those of Hanan-chacan, which is as much as to say the upper and lower waters of Cuzco, and led them in conduits; so that to this day they irrigate fields.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 19 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.

passages.text: While his ancestors had always lived in the lower part of Cuzco, and were therefore called Hurin-cuzcos, he ordered that those who sprang from him should form another party, and be called Hanan-cuzcos, which means the Cuzcos of the upper part. So that from this Inca began the party of upper or Hanan-cuzcos, for presently he and his successors left their residence at the House of the Sun, and established themselves away from it, building palaces where they lived, in the upper part of the town. It is to be noted that each Inca had a special palace in which he lived, the son not wishing to reside in the palace where his father had lived. It was left in the same state as it was in when the father died, with servants, relations, ayllus or heirs that they might maintain it, and keep the edifices in repair.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Sarmiento, History of the Incas, ch. 19 (Markham 1907); not verbatim.
